Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a workout into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme workout and deliver a live timeline: Practice Plan — Thursday AM, three lanes for one squad of twelve, three lanes, one coach
Resource limits: three lanes, one set of starting blocks, one coach on deck, two and a half hours of pool time.
Everything must be finished by 150 minutes of pool time.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Practice Plan — Thursday AM, three lanes

We have three lanes for two and a half hours and one set of starting blocks. Lane 1 is the sprint group, lane 2 the middle distance, lane 3 the distance group. Everything except the sprint set runs in all three lanes at once; the sprint set runs one lane at a time off the blocks, so lanes wait their turn.

On deck
Brief the squad on the pool deck: what the morning is, who is in which lane, 5 minutes.
Watch the warm-up from the deck and fix anything ugly; 15 minutes.

Warm-up
All three lanes start together: 20 minutes, 800 easy, mixed stroke, breathing every five on the last hundred.

Whiteboard
Call the lanes to the wall when the warm-up is done and walk the main set on the whiteboard; 5 minutes. Nobody pushes off until the board is done.

Kick set
20 minutes of kick, boards for lanes 1 and 2, vertical kick for lane 3, once the whiteboard talk is over.

Main set
Lane 1: 30 to 50 minutes, 40 minutes is the plan.
Lane 2: 30 to 50 minutes, 45 minutes is the plan.
Lane 3: 30 to 50 minutes, 50 minutes is the plan.
Every lane swims its own main set and the sprint set does not start until the last lane is in.

Sprint set
One set of blocks, one lane at a time, 10 minutes each.
Lane 1 goes first, off the blocks, dive starts, 25s flat out.
Lane 2 goes second, same thing, on the lane 1 group's last dive.
Lane 3 goes third and gets the extra rest it will need.
Time the sprints from the deck: 30 minutes, stopwatch and the wall clock.

Cooldown
All three lanes cool down together once the last sprint is in: 10 minutes, 300 easy backstroke and breaststroke.

Debrief
10 minutes on the deck at the end: splits, what to fix, Saturday's meet.

Note
The main set is the only place a lane can run long and the only place the plan gives them room to. Everything after it is a join: the blocks cannot be shared and the cooldown starts together or it does not start at all.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

This program organizes a swimming practice for a squad of twelve athletes split into three lanes over a 150-minute session. The schedule must account for sequential transitions between warm-ups, briefings, and specific sets, while managing equipment constraints—specifically, a single set of starting blocks that creates a bottleneck for the final sprint set, where lanes must cycle through individually. While most of the session involves parallel activity across all three lanes, the sprint set requires the coach to manage a one-at-a-time flow, and the entire squad must synchronize for the final cooldown and debrief. The total practice must finish within the 150-minute window, with the coach acting as the single resource coordinator on deck to manage the pacing of main sets and the rotation of the sprint blocks.

```json
{
  "summary": "A 150-minute swimming practice plan for a squad of 12 athletes across three lanes, managed by a single coach. The program synchronizes communal warm-up, briefing, and cooldown sessions with independent lane-specific training sets, while enforcing a sequential, one-at-a-time bottleneck for the sprint set due to the availability of only one set of starting blocks.",
  "servesOrScale": "12 athletes",
  "deadline": "150 minutes",
  "constraints": ["three lanes", "one set of starting blocks", "one coach", "150-minute pool time limit"]
}
```

A track represents a distinct, sequential series of activities, ensuring that concurrent tasks occur in separate parallel tracks. Each step must define a single duration—fixed, variable, or indefinite—to govern its time usage. Start triggers define the temporal dependencies of these steps, linking them to the program's beginning, a specific offset, or the completion of a previous task. To maintain consistency, every `stepId` must be globally unique across the entire program. Any `task` assigned to a step must be mirrored by a `resourceConstraints` entry, where `maxConcurrent` values enforce physical limitations on equipment or space. Finally, repeated activities should be handled by `replicates` on a single step rather than manual duplication, using `instances` and `maxInFlight` to manage dependencies and buffer capacity between chained events.

The resource constraints for this swimming practice reflect the limited deck space, the shared equipment bottleneck, and the singular oversight of the coach:

*   coach: 1 (The single actor on deck coordinating the session)
*   lanes: 3 (The three parallel swimming tracks)
*   blocks: 1 (The starting block bottleneck for the sprint set)

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "tracks are sequential lines of work; one duration kind per step; triggers link steps; every task needs a resourceConstraint; stepIds are global",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "coach", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "lanes", "maxConcurrent": 3 },
    { "task": "blocks", "maxConcurrent": 1 }
  ],
  "actors": 1
}
```

Turn 3 of 4 — extraction. Steps only: no tracks, no triggers, no program JSON.

List every timed activity you would have to perform, in the order the text gives it, with:

- a short kebab-case `stepId` and a human `name`;
- `task`: the resource it occupies while it runs — the oven, a burner, the thermocycler, the PA, the bench, your own hands. Use the same name every time for the same resource;
- how long it takes: exact (`fixed`), a range (`variable`), or "until I decide" (`indefinite`);

Split anything the text bundles into one sentence when the parts occupy different resources or different stretches of time ("brown the meat, then simmer for 40 minutes" is two activities). Do not decide yet which activities can overlap, which track they belong to, or what waits for what.

Turn 4 of 4 — relationships, then the program.

Take the step list from turn 3 exactly as it stands.

**First, tracks.** Put each step in a track: one track per parallel line of work — per dish, per station, per instrument, per performer, per sample group. Steps in one track run one after another and must not overlap; anything that runs while something else runs belongs in its own track.

**Second, triggers.** Give every step a `startTrigger` from this vocabulary and no other:

- `{"type":"programStart"}` — at t = 0.
- `{"type":"programStartOffset","offsetSeconds":n}` — n seconds after the start; this is how a short track is delayed so it finishes with the others.
- `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"x"}` — when x ends. Add `"offsetSeconds"` for a gap, `"event":"start"` to hang off x's start instead of its end, `"instances"` when x is replicated.
- `{"type":"afterStepWithBuffer","stepId":"x","bufferSeconds":n}` — n seconds after x ends.
- `{"type":"manual"}` — the person taps to start it: a gate that no clock can predict (guests seated, dough looks right, the surgeon is ready).
- `{"type":"compound","logic":"all"|"any","triggers":[...]}` — wait for all of, or the first of, several triggers.

**Third, refine the question before you answer it.** Within the scope of scheduling these activities for one person to follow, suggest a better version of the question "which activities depend on which, and which can run at the same time?" — one that would expose dependencies this text implies but does not state: things that must cool, rest, preheat, thaw, proof, be held warm, or be ready at the same moment as something else. Write your improved question out, answer it, and revise the triggers accordingly. A step the improved question reveals is added here, marked `"inferred": true`.

**Then emit the complete program JSON** in a single ```json fenced block: `schemaVersion`, `programId`, `name`, `environmentType`, `actors`, `tracks`, and a `resourceConstraints` entry for every `task` any step uses. Carry turn 3's provenance onto each step as `"metadata": {"sourceSpan": ..., "inferred": ...}`.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "0.3.0-alpha",
  "programId": "kebab-case-id",
  "name": "Human title",
  "environmentType": "kitchen",
  "actors": 2,
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "turkey",
      "name": "Turkey",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "preheat-oven",
          "name": "Preheat the oven",
          "task": "oven",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 900 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "metadata": { "sourceSpan": null, "inferred": true }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "roast-turkey",
          "name": "Roast the turkey",
          "task": "oven",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 10800 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "preheat-oven" },
          "metadata": { "sourceSpan": { "quote": "Roast the turkey for 3 hours", "occurrence": 1 }, "inferred": false }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "oven", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "counter", "maxConcurrent": 2 }
  ],
  "metadata": { "serves": "8" }
}
```

Then finish the job with the tools:
1. If the public catalog already covers this (search_public_recipes or start_workout), load that instead and stop — its result already has the live URL.
2. Otherwise keep the program you just built; `rhylthyme://guide/authoring` is the cheat-sheet and `rhylthyme://examples/*` are complete programs to pattern-match.
3. Express the limits as constraints, not as copied JSON: the `resourceConstraints`, `replicates`, `instances` and `maxInFlight` you confirmed in turn 2.
4. Run validate_program and fix every error it reports.
5. Run analyze_schedule with finishAt="150 minutes of pool time" to check the makespan, critical path and resource conflicts; adjust offsets so tracks finish together. Its `bindingConstraints` say which limit is actually gating the makespan.
6. Call visualize_schedule and give the user the live URL plus the Gantt/itinerary from the result. Do not describe the schedule in prose.
